A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the WHO and the Tanzanian national target for number of patients initiated and maintained on ART by end 2009 is unrealistic and that a more achievable target is 40% or about 175,000 patients on treatment and about 350,000 life-years (LY's) saved.

The main takeaway from our work is that

a simple dynamic model, based on the availability and productivity of staff, the time needed to initiate and maintain a patient on treatment and losses of patients, can be used to estimate the number on ART in resource-poor countries and set more realistic targets for the number on treatment.
the WHO and national targets for access to ART in Tanzania were not realistic, given the available resources.
